exposure: maternal knowledge of exclusive breastfeeding recommendations
use of bottle to give expressed milk
outcome: prevalence of exclusive breastfeeding at 6 months
prevalence of continued breastfeeding at 12 months
prevalence of continued breastfeeding at 20-24 months
cohort: The study recruited 573 mothers whose infants were aged between 12 and 24 months.
finding: The study found varying patterns of breastfeeding initiation and continuation up to 24 months, with maternal knowledge of exclusive breastfeeding duration and not using a bottle for expressed milk being associated with higher breastfeeding maintenance at 12 months.
mod_finding: Delayed initiation of breastfeeding was significantly higher in caesarean section births compared to vaginal births.
cross-section timing: When infants were aged between 12 and 24 months
